weekend_note: Next weekend (Nov 20-22) looks mild and dry through Saturday: highs in the mid 70s, with Sunday afternoon shower chances rising to about 55% per AccuWeather. Today (Sunday) is sunny and cool, and Monday may bring a few showers. Picks: EggFest today (outdoors), The Fab Four Thursday and Derek Hough Friday at the Saenger (indoors), Friday's Gallery Night and Winterfest (outdoors), and Cirque Dreams Holidaze Saturday at the Saenger (indoors). Isaias recovery still affects some places, so double-check before heading out.

news.title: Joe Vinson unseats Ashlee Hofberger in Escambia District 4 race
news.summary: After recounts and 39 late ballots, independent Vinson won by 19 votes, 13,096 to 13,077. He named Amendment 3 as his first priority.

news.title: Pensacola mayor says selling some park properties is on the table
news.summary: Mayor D.C. Reeves warned the city's general fund could shrink about 30 percent because of Amendment 3 cuts. The city reopened a renovated Dunwoody Park.

news.title: Escambia election results: penny sales tax renewal shows Yes
news.summary: WUWF's live feed also marked Sherri Myers and Boyce White as winners for Pensacola City Council. Results were from a live page and may have changed.

news.title: Nationwide FAA ground stop empties lines at Pensacola airport
news.summary: The Nov 13 stop was attributed to a telecom problem. The airport director said conditions were calm with no safety concern.

news.title: SEC keeps women's soccer championship in Pensacola two more years
news.summary: The conference extended its deal with Pensacola Sports and Escambia County. Last year's event brought about $2.6M in local revenue.

news.title: Pensacola leaders weigh phased repairs for former Gibson School
news.summary: Repairs top $6.2M. A first phase of about $2.8M would weatherproof the building; council could pick an option or defer.

news.title: SS United States sank upright off Destin after a valve delay
news.summary: The ship went down Nov 11 and rests upright about 180 feet deep, roughly 22 miles offshore.
